evals.expected_output: Starts an interactive mock interview. Presents ONE coding problem appropriate for Google L5 (medium-hard Leetcode). Asks the candidate for clarifying questions. Stays in interviewer character. Does NOT dump a solution or simulate both sides of the conversation.

assertions.name: presents-single-problem
assertions.description: Presents exactly ONE coding problem with a clear problem statement, not multiple problems at once

assertions.name: company-level-calibration
assertions.description: Problem difficulty and style is calibrated for Google L5 (medium-hard algorithmic problem, not a trivial warm-up)

assertions.name: waits-for-candidate-response
assertions.description: Ends with a question or prompt directed at the candidate (e.g., 'Do you have any clarifying questions?'), does NOT continue simulating the candidate's answers

assertions.name: stays-in-interviewer-character
assertions.description: Maintains interviewer persona throughout — does not break character to explain the skill or give meta-instructions

assertions.name: does-not-reveal-solution
assertions.description: Does NOT provide the solution, optimal approach, or complexity analysis upfront — waits for candidate to work through it

evals.expected_output: Presents a code snippet with a subtle bug. Does NOT reveal the bug. Uses Socratic method to guide the candidate. Asks questions instead of giving answers.

assertions.name: presents-buggy-code
assertions.description: Shows a code snippet that contains a subtle, non-obvious bug (not a syntax error)

assertions.name: bug-not-revealed
assertions.description: Does NOT tell the candidate what the bug is or where it is located

assertions.name: socratic-method
assertions.description: Asks guiding questions to help the candidate find the bug themselves, rather than explaining directly

assertions.name: waits-for-candidate
assertions.description: Ends with a question for the candidate, does not simulate the debugging process on both sides

evals.expected_output: Starts a system design interview. Presents a high-level design problem appropriate for Meta Senior level. Asks about requirements and constraints first. One question at a time.

assertions.name: presents-design-problem
assertions.description: Presents a high-level system design problem (e.g., 'Design Instagram', 'Design a News Feed') appropriate for Meta Senior

assertions.name: asks-about-requirements-first
assertions.description: Asks or prompts the candidate to discuss requirements, constraints, or scope before diving into architecture

assertions.name: one-question-at-a-time
assertions.description: Does not dump a full list of design topics — asks one question or addresses one aspect at a time

assertions.name: meta-senior-calibration
assertions.description: Problem scale and depth expectations match Meta Senior level (large-scale distributed systems, not a simple CRUD app)
